The company has stated that it processes browsing and behavioural data on a large scale for behavioural advertising, that the people affected are its customers, and that its interest in the processing is commercial. It also markets to them through online advertising. In its decision on LinkedIn, the Irish Data Protection Commission found that LinkedIn could not rely on legitimate interests under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR for this kind of processing — analysing members' data to target them with ads — because the rights and interests of the people affected outweighed LinkedIn's own interests. That decision weighs against the company's position here. But the outcome depends on this company's own facts: its purposes, the data involved, its safeguards, the effects on people, and what those people could reasonably expect. Section IV weighs those facts. (DPC, Inquiry into LinkedIn Ireland Unlimited Company, decision of 22 October 2024, § 7; decision of a lead supervisory authority applying the GDPR.)
